meta.title: X Content Learning Loop
meta.decisionQuestion: Which feedback may change the next round without bypassing human authority or safety gates?

sources.label: Sanitized X workflow synthesis
claims: Content loops need feedback, authority, receipts, and rollback

nodes.title: Observe
nodes.summary: Collect candidate topics and context without deciding what to publish.
decisions: Keep collection separate from publishing authority
risks: A noisy source can dominate the queue

nodes.title: Classify
nodes.summary: Choose topic, audience, format, and risk class for the next attempt.
risks: Classification errors can scale into repeated bad output

nodes.title: Draft
nodes.summary: Create a bounded candidate, not an irreversible public action.
risks: Fluent output can hide weak evidence

nodes.title: Verify
nodes.summary: Check claims, voice, media, policy, and failure conditions.
decisions: Fail closed on unsupported material claims
risks: A single aggregate score can hide a critical failure

nodes.title: Autonomy gate
nodes.summary: Decide whether this action needs approval or fits a pre-authorized envelope.
risks: Silent scope expansion removes human authority

nodes.title: Publish
nodes.summary: Execute the external action only after the gate resolves.
decisions: Attach a receipt to every external action
risks: Provider failure can strand scheduled work

nodes.title: Measure
nodes.summary: Collect outcome signals separately from the system's own confidence.
risks: Fast metrics can reward shallow reactions

nodes.title: Learn
nodes.summary: Propose what should change next; do not directly rewrite accepted policy.
risks: Self-reinforcement can amplify a bad proxy

nodes.title: Human review
nodes.summary: Approves high-risk or out-of-envelope actions and resolves dissent.
risks: Review can become a bottleneck without clear thresholds

nodes.title: Kill switch
nodes.summary: Stops external action without waiting for the learning loop.
decisions: Keep stop authority outside the autonomous path
risks: A hidden or slow stop is not a real control

nodes.title: Stale-data guard
nodes.summary: Blocks classification when inputs are too old or provenance is missing.
decisions: Prefer an explicit degraded mode over silent freshness loss
risks: Healthy infrastructure can still carry stale meaning

nodes.title: Receipts
nodes.summary: Record what was checked, approved, executed, and observed.
risks: Logs without stable IDs cannot prove causality

nodes.title: Policy store
nodes.summary: Holds the current autonomy envelope and accepted decision history.
decisions: Accepted policy changes only through a superseding decision
risks: Mutable policy erases why the system changed

nodes.title: Rollback
nodes.summary: Restores the last accepted policy or removes a queued external action.
risks: A rollback plan can fail if receipts are incomplete

edges.label: candidate packet
edges.impact: Fresh observations give classification something current to act on.
edges.ifRemoved: The loop drafts from stale memory.

edges.label: content brief
edges.impact: A bounded brief tells drafting what job to perform.
edges.ifRemoved: Drafting becomes an unscoped text generator.

edges.label: candidate bundle
edges.ifRemoved: There is no inspectable object to approve.

edges.label: verification receipt
edges.impact: The autonomy gate needs explicit quality and safety results.
edges.ifRemoved: Fluent output can pass without evidence.

edges.label: authority
edges.impact: Publishing requires approval or a matching pre-authorized envelope.
edges.ifRemoved: The system can widen its own authority.

edges.label: observable outcome
edges.impact: Only an executed action can produce external outcome signals.

edges.label: outcome packet
edges.ifRemoved: Learning follows the model's opinion of itself.

edges.label: next-round hypothesis
edges.impact: Learning changes the next classification hypothesis, closing the loop.
edges.ifRemoved: The workflow is a pipeline, not a learning system.

edges.label: freshness check
edges.impact: Stale or untraceable inputs stop the loop before selection.
edges.ifRemoved: The system can confidently act on expired context.

edges.label: explicit approval
edges.impact: High-risk actions require an affirmative human event.
edges.ifRemoved: Silence can be interpreted as consent.

edges.label: stop signal
edges.impact: The operator can stop execution outside the loop's normal cadence.
edges.ifRemoved: The system has no reliable emergency brake.

edges.label: execution receipt
edges.ifRemoved: The team cannot prove what actually happened.

edges.label: recovery evidence
edges.impact: Rollback needs stable IDs and the previous accepted state.

edges.label: restore boundary
edges.impact: Rollback returns the system to the last accepted authority boundary.
edges.ifRemoved: A failed experiment can permanently widen authority.

edges.label: current envelope
edges.impact: Classification must respect the accepted autonomy policy.
edges.ifRemoved: The next round can ignore agreed limits.

edges.label: superseding proposal
edges.impact: Learning may propose a policy change but cannot accept it.
edges.ifRemoved: The loop cannot improve its authority model.

edges.label: outcome receipt
edges.impact: Outcome evidence remains tied to the action that caused it.

decisions.title: Choose approval-by-default or bounded autonomy by risk class
decisions.context: The loop needs speed without giving itself unlimited publishing authority.
decisions.rationale: Start with bounded autonomy and explicit escalation outside the envelope.
tradeoffs: Lower review load for routine actions
consequences: Every action needs a risk class and authority receipt

decisions.title: Allow learning to propose policy changes but not accept them
decisions.context: A self-editing loop can reinforce a bad metric or proxy.
decisions.rollbackPlan: Disable learning proposals and restore the last accepted policy.

decisions.title: Choose fail-closed or labeled degraded mode when evidence is stale
decisions.context: Inputs and metrics can be missing even when infrastructure appears healthy.
decisions.rationale: Never continue silently; choose between the first two by risk class.
consequences: Freshness status becomes a gate input

reviews.finding: The autonomy envelope needs explicit risk classes and decision ownership.
Stable action and event IDs are required for metrics, rollback, and audit.
Stop authority and privacy checks must remain outside the self-modifying loop.
Learning may propose changes, but accepted policy must remain append-only and human-owned.
